extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (authors) and peer reviewers considering submission to eLife (life/biomedical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Description of eLife's Reviewed Preprint publishing and peer-review workflow, what reviewers and editors are required to produce, and how assessments and public reviews are published and updated across versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication model: Reviewed Preprints published for all reviewed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: At eLife we do not accept or reject papers after peer review: rather, every paper we review is published on the eLife website as a Reviewed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Reviewed Preprint combines the authors' preprint and feedback from experts; the journal's model ensures that manuscripts selected for peer review are published regardless of outcome of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor selection for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife editors — who are all active researchers — discuss new submissions and decide which will be peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific criteria used by editors are discussed in 'How and why eLife selects papers for peer review' (linked from the page). Editors perform an initial selection step before external peer review is commissioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each peer reviewer must write a Public Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer reviewer is asked to write a Public Review of the article, and to recommend ways in which the authors could improve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Reviews are part of the published Reviewed Preprint; reviewers should describe strengths and weaknesses and provide concrete recommendations for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment summarises significance and strength of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor and the peer reviewers also write an eLife Assessment that summarises the significance of the findings and the strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assessment is a concise summary produced by editors and reviewers and is published alongside the preprint and Public Reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of common vocabulary for assessment scales
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife Assessments use a common vocabulary to summarise the significance of the findings (on a scale ranging from landmark to useful) and the strength of the evidence (on a scale ranging exceptional to inadequate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should place the work on these standard scales to give readers a consistent sense of impact and evidential strength across papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Reviews must indicate whether claims and conclusions are justified by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Reviews describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly assess the extent to which the presented data support the authors' claims; such judgements are published for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit reporting of reviewer disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reviewers disagree with the claims in an article, this is made explicit within the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreements among reviewers are not hidden; the Assessment and Public Reviews should record differing views so readers see the range of expert opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of a Reviewed Preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: A Reviewed Preprint includes the preprint itself, the eLife Assessment, Public Reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and a response from the authors (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When published these elements are presented together so the paper and the expert commentary are integrated in the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of revised versions and updated assessments/reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to submit a revised version of their article when they are ready, and the editor and the peer reviewers will update the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version two of the Reviewed Preprint will include the revised preprint, an updated eLife Assessment and Public Reviews (as appropriate), and a response from the authors — reviewers and editors must re-evaluate and update their published commentary to reflect changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to publish a Version of Record (VOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point following peer review, the authors can choose to publish their article as a regular journal article (the Version of Record) to mark the end of the review and publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A VOR complies with major funder requirements for immediate online access and is typically indexed by multiple services (though indexing cannot be guaranteed). Choosing a VOR marks finalization of the review lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations to authors are part of the published record
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to the authors for improving the article are published as part of the Version of Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions suggested by reviewers/editors are not private; they become part of the permanent published record so readers can see suggested improvements and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint availability policy for submissions selected for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife works with authors to make all submissions selected for peer review available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making a submission public as a preprint is built into the process for papers that are selected for peer review, increasing transparency and early access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our publication fee is $2,500 and is payable at this stage (although the fee is waived for anyone who cannot afford to pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of the fee at the peer-review stage and that eLife provides waivers for those who cannot pay; this is a practical requirement for publication under this model.
